stem: A client is transferred from the emergency department to an inpatient unit after receiving a new IV antibiotic and being identified as high fall risk. What should the handoff include?

options.A: Provide the new room number without additional clinical detail because the receiving nurse can locate the remaining information in the electronic record.
options.B: Communicate current clinical status, treatment given, pending information, fall risk and precautions, and allow the receiving nurse to clarify questions.
options.C: Provide billing, insurance, and transport details while omitting most clinical information because the chart already contains the medical record.
options.D: Skip direct handoff communication because transferring responsibility through the electronic chart alone is sufficient without acknowledgment by the receiver.

rationale: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS defines handoff as transfer of information together with authority and responsibility during transitions in care. Effective handoff includes current condition, response to treatment, recent changes, the plan and contingencies, receiver acknowledgment, and an opportunity to ask questions. B therefore best transfers the clinically relevant status, treatment, pending information and safety precautions. A and C omit essential clinical information, and D incorrectly assumes an electronic record alone is sufficient without acknowledgment.
educational_objective: Provide a complete, acknowledged handoff that transfers clinically relevant information, safety concerns and responsibility during care transitions.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)

source_claim_supported: A safe handoff transfers current clinical information and responsibility, requires acknowledgment and permits clarification/questions.

source_original.stem: A client is transferred from the emergency department to an inpatient unit after receiving a new IV antibiotic and being identified as high fall risk. What should the handoff include?

options.A: Provide the new room number without additional clinical detail because the receiving nurse can locate the remaining information in the electronic record.
options.B: Communicate current clinical status, treatment given, pending information, fall risk and precautions, and allow the receiving nurse to clarify questions.
options.C: Provide billing, insurance, and transport details while omitting most clinical information because the chart already contains the medical record.
options.D: Skip direct handoff communication because transferring responsibility through the electronic chart alone is sufficient without acknowledgment by the receiver.

source_original.rationale: A safe handoff transfers the information, responsibility, and accountability needed for the receiving team to continue care. Option B is correct because it communicates current status, treatment, pending information, fall risk and precautions, and supports clarification. Option A supplies only a location. Option C omits clinically essential information. Option D incorrectly assumes electronic documentation alone replaces acknowledged handoff communication.
source_original.source_detail: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS — Communication Module, Handoff: standardized transfer of information and responsibility/accountability during transitions; effective handoff conveys current condition, care/treatment and action/contingency information, requires receiver acknowledgment, and permits clarification/questions. correction_summary: Retained construct/key; upgraded source locator to AHRQ's dedicated Handoff tool and kept the item focused on clinically relevant transition information and acknowledged transfer.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Fall risk/precautions are appropriate safety information within a handoff; no institution-specific mnemonic mandated.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B includes the relevant content and clarification opportunity.
